display.title: Episode 205: The Great Surprise, Chapter 1
display.summary_short: Tzivos Hashem soldiers in Alaska, a young guest from Australia who recites the Shema and the Ten Commandments, and the start of the story of a poor sand seller whose horse and wagon are stolen.
display.summary_long: Uncle Yossi opens with the new Moshiach Times magazine and its field report from Tzivos Hashem members in Anchorage, Alaska, who visit a zoo, paddle a kayak and dig in a gold mine, remembering that every Jew is like a gold mine of good character and good deeds. After the Hakochainik march to 'Hinei Mah Tov', he gives a number to check the mezuzah contest winners' list and tells listeners in Kew Gardens Hills where a sofer will gladly show them a real mezuzah. A young guest who flew in from Sydney, Australia, leads the Shema and recites the opening of the Ten Commandments by heart. Story time begins 'The Great Surprise': Rabbi Yitzchak, a learned and pious man, earns a meager living selling fresh sand from the forest with his squeaky old wagon, yet sets aside coins for tzedakah every day. One stormy night a thief steals his horse and wagon. Rabbi Yitzchak calms his family, reminding them that whatever Hashem does is for the good, and they sit down to say Tehillim. A great miracle is about to happen, to be continued next week. The show ends with details of the Wonderful World of Shabbos exhibit.
display.lesson: Whatever Hashem does is for the good; even in hard times we trust Him and turn to Him in prayer.
